queue.title: Tabby: An Open Pretraining Recipe for Time Series Foundation Models
queue.claim: From the title only (page not fetched): an open pretraining recipe for pretrained forecasting models, with weights.
queue.why_relevant: The spec lists Tabby as a univariate wrapper; sktime 1.3.0 also added it.

queue.title: TabPFN-3.5: Technical Report
queue.claim: A new tabular foundation model release that reports stronger time-series forecasting through task-specific harnesses.
queue.why_relevant: TabPFN-TS-style forecasting with covariates may build on it; the abstract gives no load result.

queue.title: Medium-Term Multi-Resolution Electric Load Forecasting using Economic Data and Foundation Model
queue.claim: From the title only (page not fetched): medium-term electric load at several resolutions using economic data and a foundation model.
queue.why_relevant: Electric load with covariates and a pretrained model; longer horizon than the spec.

queue.title: Foundation or Formula? A Simulation-Based Comparison of Google's TimesFM-3 and Classical Time-Series Models
queue.claim: On 7200 simulated series under a pre-registered 12-step protocol neither family dominates: TimesFM-3 is never more than 1.31 times the best method, while automatic ARIMA is 21-24% more accurate on seasonal data with four or more cycles.
queue.why_relevant: Pre-registered comparison of a new foundation model with classical baselines on data it cannot have seen; synthetic series, not load.

queue.title: Zero-shot time-series foundation models against the Khepri v1.5 baselines for 96-hour carbon-intensity forecasts in nine Nordic bidding zones: a preregistered comparison
queue.claim: A preregistered 96-hour comparison in nine Nordic zones: three zero-shot models beat SARIMA and GBM baselines on the 2025 test, but the holdout difference was inconclusive.
queue.why_relevant: Pre-registered multi-day hourly energy-series backtest of zero-shot models; carbon intensity rather than load.

queue.title: Forecasting Daily Household Electricity Demand in a Hot-Arid City: A Comparative Benchmark of Local, Global, Deep and Foundation Models on ESHED-38
queue.claim: On daily smart-meter data for 38 homes with 48 weekly origins and lead times up to 30 days, the best of 24 configurations cut seasonal-naive error by 20 to 25%, with zero-shot Chronos-2 among the leaders.
queue.why_relevant: Weekly origins and multi-week lead times with weather, on household rather than zonal load.
queue.query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

queue.title: IBM Granite Time Series PatchTST-FM-r2
queue.claim: A 385M-parameter Apache-2.0 zero-shot model ranked top among permissively licensed replicable models on GIFT-Eval as of 8 September 2026; the page does not mention covariates.
queue.why_relevant: Open univariate forecasting model that could run on load history only.

queue.title: Zero-shot forecasting models and GB electricity demand: a preregistered test
queue.claim: Without weather inputs, zero-shot Chronos-2 and Timestral-209M beat a weekly-lag regression on day-ahead GB demand by roughly 7 to 9 percent over 2024-01 to 2026-10, short of the 10 percent gain set in advance, and TimesFM 2.5 was no better than the regression.
queue.why_relevant: The study our backtest design mirrors: pretrained models against a lag regression on national load with a preregistered 10 percent bar, univariate and day-ahead.
queue.query: TimesFM OR Chronos-2 OR Timestral OR TabPFN-TS electricity load

queue.title: TimesFM 3.0: natively multivariate zero-shot forecasting with covariates
queue.claim: Google released TimesFM 3.0, a 330M-parameter model that forecasts several targets jointly with past-only and known-future covariates in one pass, and reports the best average rank among pretrained models on GIFT-Eval, fev-bench and TIME; the weights carry a non-commercial licence.
queue.why_relevant: A model that takes temperature as a known-future covariate and is listed as ff_native_exog; its weights date falls inside our scored window.

queue.title: Physics-Informed Fractional Load Forecasting With Memory-Aware Break Detection for Reserve Scheduling
queue.claim: A day-ahead load model with a fractional temperature kernel for building thermal inertia and joint estimation of breaks and long memory improves on the best of ten benchmarks by 15.7% and 10.3% MAPE on New England and Mid-Atlantic data.
queue.why_relevant: A temperature-driven regression-style load model tested on Mid-Atlantic load, the region of our PJM zones; day-ahead rather than week-ahead.

queue.title: Zero-shot foundation models on Belgian day-ahead electricity load
queue.claim: Over the 365 days of 2025, zero-shot Chronos-2 and Timestral with calendar and previous-day temperature forecasts reach a day-ahead error on Belgian load about level with the grid operator's own forecast, within the confidence intervals.
queue.why_relevant: Chronos-2 and Timestral with forecast (not observed) temperature on national load over a full year, at day-ahead rather than week-ahead.
queue.query: TimesFM OR Chronos-2 OR Timestral OR TabPFN-TS electricity load

queue.title: TimeH2O v1 (H2O.ai)
queue.claim: H2O.ai published open weights for a pretrained forecasting model, TimeH2O v1; the model card was not read, so no accuracy claim is recorded here.
queue.why_relevant: spec.yaml lists TimeH2O as runnable with temperature through FoundationForecast, so it could be measured on our benchmark; weights fall inside the scored window.

queue.title: The Hidden Look-Ahead: Point-in-Time Leakage in Electricity Market Data
queue.claim: For ten weather-model configurations matched to GB auction gates over 2022 to 2026, choosing the latest forecast run issued before the gate picks a run not yet published on most delivery days for six of them, with an accuracy effect that varies in sign and size.
queue.why_relevant: A check on the no-lookahead rule for our forecast-weather regime (lead-matched archived forecasts); it audits inputs and does not forecast load.

queue.title: Timer-M1: A Multivariate Time Series Foundation Model via Learning Primitives
queue.claim: Timer-M1, a pretrained multivariate model trained with explicit target, past-only and known-future covariate roles, is reported first on the FEV and TIME benchmarks and second on GIFT-Eval.
queue.why_relevant: A pretrained model designed for known-future covariates; no load result and not among the models we can run today.

queue.title: Chronos-2 LoRA adapter for European hourly load
queue.claim: A LoRA adapter for Chronos-2 tuned on 2015 to 2017 hourly load from five European countries reports a mean MASE of 0.387 against 0.402 for zero-shot Chronos-2 on 2019 day-ahead forecasts.
queue.why_relevant: A load-specific variant of the model in our primary comparison; day-ahead, European, and the card does not say whether covariates are used.

queue.title: Hybrid deep learning models for medium-term electricity load forecasting
queue.claim: A hybrid residual model reaches about 4% MAPE for hourly demand at horizons of 720 to 2160 hours on one dataset, using climatological averages in place of future weather.
queue.why_relevant: Hourly load at horizons beyond a week with an explicit rule against using future weather; one dataset.
queue.query: week-ahead OR medium-term electricity load forecasting

queue.title: A Later Test Set Is Not a New Domain: Pretraining Familiarity Survives a Contamination-Free Hold-Out
queue.claim: On data published after every model's release, pretrained forecasters win five of seven groups, and their advantage tracks how familiar the domain is from the pretraining corpus rather than seasonal strength or spectral entropy.
queue.why_relevant: Speaks to our weights rule (weeks after weights): a post-release window may not remove domain familiarity; not about load.

queue.title: A survey and benchmark for household electricity forecasting: From statistical to foundation models
queue.claim: A benchmark of 30 models from statistical to foundation models on household load, PV and battery series, with public code.
queue.why_relevant: Includes zero-shot foundation models on electricity load; household level, and no headline number in the search summary.
queue.query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

queue.title: Ranking reliability in building level day ahead load forecasting: analysis code
queue.claim: Sixteen forecasters including pretrained foundation models are evaluated under a ten-origin and a 238-origin protocol to measure how window length and the number of compared models change the reliability of rankings.
queue.why_relevant: Evidence on how many origins a load-forecast ranking needs, which bears on our 52-origin design.

queue.title: ElecLoad: Adaptive Electricity Load Forecasting Guided by Multiple Events
queue.claim: A context-aware agent that reads notices, weather alerts and event schedules and splits the forecast horizon by event effects is reported as the most accurate method in most scenarios on several load datasets.
queue.why_relevant: Electric load forecasting with weather-related context, but through text events and an LLM agent rather than a temperature series, and unlikely to run on a CPU laptop.

queue.title: OpenSTEF 4.0: modular short-term energy forecasting with a foundation-model forecaster and a backtesting framework
queue.claim: OpenSTEF 4.0 adds a learned ensemble of forecasters, a foundation-model forecaster and a backtesting and evaluation package designed to keep model comparisons free of future-data leakage.
queue.why_relevant: An open load-forecasting library used by grid operators that now ships a foundation-model forecaster and a backtest harness.

queue.title: Adaptive Residual Modeling for Scenario Learning in Probabilistic Load Forecasting
queue.claim: A two-stage scenario model for feeder active and reactive power with a separate tail-calibration step cuts the 0.99-quantile pinball loss by roughly 30 to 85 percent against three baselines on one feeder dataset.
queue.why_relevant: Probabilistic load forecasting with an environmental-response component, at feeder level and about extreme quantiles rather than zonal week-ahead error.

queue.title: From Shared Demand Patterns to Local Uncertainty: Probabilistic Load Forecasting by Mixing Compact Adaptations
queue.claim: A shared forecaster with a small bank of low-dimensional adapters mixed per load improves point and probabilistic accuracy over statistical, neural and pretrained baselines on 590 synthetic-grid load profiles.
queue.why_relevant: Load forecasting compared against pretrained baselines, at customer and transformer level on a synthetic dataset.

queue.title: Probabilistic electrical power demand forecasting with uncertainty quantification
queue.claim: Among four probabilistic methods compared on zonal power-consumption data, NGBoost gives the lowest errors and well-covered, fairly narrow intervals.
queue.why_relevant: Zonal electricity consumption, but the abstract names no dataset, horizon or weather input, and no pretrained model.

queue.title: SAP-RPT-TS: SAP's time series foundation model
queue.claim: SAP announced a roughly 28M-parameter zero-shot forecasting model with past and future covariates and claims the lowest MASE and scaled quantile loss among the models it shows on fev-bench.
queue.why_relevant: A covariate-aware model whose worked example is building energy with temperature as a future covariate; offered through SAP services with no open weights mentioned.

queue.title: Zero-shot time series foundation models for statistical postprocessing of weather forecasts: analysis code
queue.claim: The record holds the code of a study that uses TimesFM-3 and Chronos-2 zero-shot, with the ensemble mean as a covariate, to post-process 2 m temperature forecasts at German stations and compares them with statistical methods; the record itself gives no result.
queue.why_relevant: Pretrained models with a known-future covariate on the temperature input our forecast regime depends on; the target is weather, not load.

queue.title: SPECTRA: State-Space Exogenous Context and Temporal-Frequency Resolution Architecture for Probabilistic Energy Forecasting
queue.claim: An architecture that separates deterministic and residual streams and aligns exogenous context with both achieves the best CRPS in 14 of 18 load, price, solar and wind settings, 5.74% below the strongest baselines on average.
queue.why_relevant: Probabilistic load forecasting with exogenous inputs including temperature; a trained architecture, not a zero-shot model.

queue.title: BQEB ForecastBench: Benchmarking AI Models for Smart Grid Forecasting Using BQEB-Data v1
queue.claim: On an open smart-grid dataset with a chronological split, linear regression beats random forest and gradient boosting for both next-hour load and day-ahead price forecasting.
queue.why_relevant: A reproducible load benchmark in which a plain regression wins, but at a one-hour horizon with no pretrained model.
queue.query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

queue.title: A controlled benchmark of temporal dependence for day-ahead electricity-demand discrepancies in Great Britain
queue.claim: A retrospective benchmark over 364 days of 2024 compares independent, Gaussian-copula and empirical ensembles of GB day-ahead demand-forecast discrepancies on shared marginals and keeps its adverse and inconclusive findings.
queue.why_relevant: About the time dependence of day-ahead demand forecast errors, which matters for scoring multi-hour windows; it does not forecast load itself.

queue.title: Evaluating Accuracy and Probabilistic Reliability of Zero-Shot Time Series Foundation Models
queue.claim: Six zero-shot foundation models beat statistical baselines and a supervised model on energy, traffic and financial data but trade point accuracy against calibration, with patch-based transformers miscalibrated at long horizons.
queue.why_relevant: Zero-shot models on energy series across horizons; no covariates and no load-specific result in the abstract.
queue.query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

queue.title: Thaki EnergyLoad Forecaster v0.1
queue.claim: Three LightGBM models for a single meter's load at 15-minute, 1-hour and 24-hour horizons, trained on a public 2011 to 2014 Portuguese dataset, report lower MASE than the best simple baseline on a six-month hold-out.
queue.why_relevant: Electric load forecasting with a model family we already run, but per-meter, without weather inputs and at most a day ahead.

queue.title: When Do Time Series Foundation Models Help Forecast Wind Energy Droughts? A Preregistered Evaluation (code and results)
queue.claim: A preregistered study evaluates Chronos-2, TimesFM 2.5 and Moirai-2 with NWP covariates against climatology, model output statistics, quantile regression and a recurrent network for cumulative wind energy deficit in 16 regions.
queue.why_relevant: Preregistered test of foundation models with forecast-weather covariates on an energy series; wind rather than load, and the record summary gives no result.
